description: a small engraved circle, about five pixels across, standing beside a name in lower case
reason: a circle has one centre and the engraver put it where the place is

description: the same circle at the centre of a small walled block, with a cross rising from it, beside a name in capitals
anchor_point: the centre of the circle inside the block
reason: the block and the cross are attributes - a walled town, an episcopal see - drawn AROUND the same position circle. Verified at eight times magnification on Porto, Braga, Lamego, Viseu, Coimbra and Braganca before any of them was used

description: a perspective drawing of a town
reason: no defensible centre. This is why the 1762 sheet was refused in MAPGEN-027 and is still refused here

description: a bastioned star drawn in plan, as at Castelo Branco and Castro Marim
reason: a plan of the works, not the conventional position mark. Its centroid is the centre of the enceinte, which is not what the plate's own circle means. Castelo Branco therefore yields no anchor even though its name is perfectly legible

description: the bowl of an engraved o, e or a
reason: the same size and weight as a town circle at this scale. Three readings locked onto lettering and were caught at magnification; two were corrected to the sign and one was struck out

description: a stroke on the sheet border at every ten minutes
anchor_point: the stroke, in ONE coordinate only
reason: a longitude stroke fixes longitude and says nothing about latitude. Crossing one with a latitude stroke to manufacture a pixel is what MAPGEN-018R disqualified and is not done here
